title: Latin America on Film
description: An exploration of Latin American film and how this medium represents the cultures, histories and politics of the region. We will study a selection of films encompassing different genres, styles and historical periods, including some key works by influential Latin American filmmakers.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 16B or Spanish 25

title: Lorca, Tradition, Modernity, and the Avant Garde
description: A study of Lorcas poetry and theater in the context of the major artistic, sociopolitical and historical transformations of the early 20th century, exploring how traditional Spanish culture and avant-garde innovation intersect each other in his work.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently)

title: The Hispanic Novel and Cinema
description: Study of three or four Hispanic novels vis-a-vis their film versions, permitting analysis of narrative in both genres, using existing films and videos based on masterpieces of Hispanic literature. Taught in Spanish.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently).

title: Contemporary Spanish Cultural Studies
description: An interdisciplinary approach to the understanding of present-day Spain, focusing on popular music, TV and literature from the 1960s until today.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L OR Span 30. (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently.)

title: Spanish-American Thought
description: Leading social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends from the sixteenth century to the present.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 16B or Spanish 25

title: Science Fiction in Latin America
description: An exploration of science fiction narrative and film from Latin America. Through a selection of works by Latin American authors from the early 20th century until the present, we will study how the history, cultures, and traditions of the region have shaped the genre of science fiction, and how this affords a singular perspective to think about topics like technology, neoliberalism, ethnicity, colonialism, the environment, and the future of the planet.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 30 or Spanish 102L (may be taken concurrently).

description: Study of Hispanic literature by author or special topics.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

title: Moving Bodies: Stories of Migration
description: Analyzes the experience of migration and diaspora formation by focusing on how the Basque settled in the American West.

title: Gender in Basque Culture
description: Using Basque culture as a case study, this course explores how gender intersects with other crucial issues such as ethnicity, nationhood, and globalization.

title: Central American Literature and Culture
description: Addresses the issues of Central American literature and culture as a way of encompassing the entire Central American region consisting of 7 countries (Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Panama). Part of the emphasis is to examine the larger area but also specific points of the respective countries. Concentration will be on the cultural productions of such countries (specifically literature) but will include history, geopolitics, geography, folklore, and others.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

title: Conflict, Memory, and Cultural Production
description: Explores how cultural artifacts like novels and films articulate individual and collective histories of violence.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

title: Basque Studies through Literature and Culture in Translation (Spanish/English)
description: Delves deeper into the diversity of topics that make up Basque Studies, and analyses historical, but also contemporary socio-cultural topics related to the Basque country and the Basque diaspora abroad. Can be taken either as a continuation of SPAN 153E or a self-standing course on Basque Studies, where literary and cultural materials are presented in their English, Spanish, and possibly also French translations depending on student interest and language choice.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).

title: Transnational Perspectives in the 19th Century: Spain/Cuba/U.S.
description: A study through literary texts of the political, cultural, and economic interrelations between Spain, Cuba, and the U.S. during the 19th century, from the Wars of Independence until the 1898 Spanish-American War.
prerequisites_raw: Spanish 102L or Spanish 30 (may be taken concurrently).
